channel.title: Sunward
channel.description: Only good news. Each morning Sunward reads real newsrooms, keeps the stories where something got better, and says why in one line.

item.title: This Blue Whale Population Grew 1,000% Since the End of Antarctic Whaling
item.description: Antarctic blue whales have grown from 418 to about 4,000 since whaling stopped in 1973. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Empire State Building Lit Up with Gold Marks Historic Milestone of NASA’s Voyager 1 This Week
item.description: Voyager 1 is now one light-day from Earth and still sending signals home, 49 years after launch. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Over 100 Cave Bear Skeletons Found in ‘Sensational’ Discovery by Alpine Guide
item.description: An Alpine guide found a cave holding over 100 cave bear skeletons, kept secret so looters stay away. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked
item.description: Five centuries-old baobabs stopped from illegal export are being replanted in South Africa. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: Something strange is living beneath the skin of deep-sea pigs
item.description: Scientists found a new bacterium living in partnership beneath the skin of deep-sea sea pigs. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: The Waterless, Hyper-Efficient Machines That Clean Clothes With Carbon Dioxide
item.description: New washing machines clean clothes with recycled carbon dioxide instead of water and heat. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Students Fighting to Save Poached Plant Species That Only Exists in Near Their Campus
item.description: Students and scientists are working to save a wildflower that grows only in their valley after poachers took plants. How you can help: Buy succulents from nurseries that grow their own stock, never plants dug from the wild. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Siblings Build 430-Step ‘Sky Ladder’ for Their Mother Who Refuses to Live in the City
item.description: Siblings built 430 steps up a mountain by hand so their mother can keep living in her home. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: ‘Huge experiment in biogeography’: US offshore windfarms are creating artificial reefs
item.description: Offshore windfarm foundations are turning into reefs full of sea life, and scientists are studying them. Evidence: Early research. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: Scientists ‘Cure’ Deadly Brain Tumors in Every Mouse Tested with New Cancer Therapy
item.description: A new immune cell therapy cleared an aggressive childhood brain cancer in every mouse tested. Evidence: Early research. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: New discovery reveals what may be holding back room-temperature superconductors
item.description: A key ingredient of superconductivity was found to survive at room temperature, a clue for lossless power. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: 125,000 years ago, hippos roamed what is now the vast Arabian Desert
item.description: Stone tools and plant remains show the Arabian Desert once held lakes, hippos and thriving early humans. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: US homelessness decline hits its steepest one-year drop in a decade
item.description: US homelessness fell over 6% in 2025, about 49,000 fewer people, the steepest drop in a decade. Evidence: Proven at scale. How you can help: Ask your local shelter what it needs this winter; coats and socks often run short. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: April Surac built NeuraSensa so art adapts to the people using it
item.description: A young designer built NeuraSensa, art installations that adapt to each visitor’s senses. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Pakistan's solar revolution is so successful the national grid is lagging behind
item.description: Rooftop solar has lifted Pakistan's solar share of electricity from 1% to 28%. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: West Coast’s First Ever Sea Turtle Hatchlings Released into the Pacific (LOOK)
item.description: Olive ridley hatchlings from the first sea turtle nest recorded on the US West Coast reached the Pacific. How you can help: Give nesting turtles space on beaches and report any nest to local wildlife officials. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: William and Kate celebrate Earthshot Prize winners in Mumbai
item.description: This year’s Earthshot Prize honoured environmental innovators at a ceremony in Mumbai. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: Algeria Returns Kindness Shown by Kansans Who Welcomed its World Cup Team with the Trip of a Lifetime
item.description: Algeria flew out Kansas families who had hosted its World Cup team and gave them the welcome back. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Warren Buffett Gives Away $5.5 Billion in Thanksgiving Gift, Saying Kindness Is Priceless
item.description: Warren Buffett gave about $5.5 billion in shares to charity in his yearly Thanksgiving gift. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Largest Electric Bus Fleet in New York to Serve Bronx Neighborhood Elevated Asthma Rates
item.description: New York's largest electric school bus fleet now runs in a South Bronx area with high child asthma rates. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Can this experimental orchard save the UK’s cider industry?
item.description: A Somerset orchard is testing apple varieties and methods to keep cider trees healthy as climate shifts. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: The Greek coastline cleanup that turned trash into a pollution map
item.description: A cleanup on a small Greek islet logged every item found, building a map of where marine litter comes from. How you can help: Join a beach cleanup and log what you find; the records help track pollution. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Animal welfare ballot measures had a strong night in the 2026 midterms
item.description: US voters passed several animal welfare measures on 3 November by wide margins. Evidence: Now policy. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Farmer Finds Unknown Seeds in His Attic – and Grows an Ancient ‘Miracle’ Grain
item.description: A Parma farmer grew an old wheat variety from seeds he found in his attic, reviving a lost grain. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: 30% Drop in Levels of Forever Chemicals in England’s Rivers, 49% in Fish – ‘Brilliant to See’
item.description: Two banned forever chemicals have fallen about 30% in England's rivers and nearly half in fish. Evidence: Now policy. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: NASA is offering $1 million for bold ideas to help build a Moon base
item.description: NASA is offering $1 million for student ideas on building the first permanent Moon base. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Tokyo Tackles Trash Troubles with New Generation of Robotic Street Waste Bins
item.description: Tokyo is trying solar compacting bins and robot haulers to keep tourist streets clean. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Climbers Lug Endangered and Orphaned Seal Pup Up a Cliff to Safety
item.description: Climbers in Greece carried an orphaned, critically endangered monk seal pup up a cliff to rescuers. How you can help: If you find a seal pup alone on a beach, keep your distance and call a wildlife rescue line. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Hidden ecosystem: Scientists discover 245 animals living inside a single deep-sea rock
item.description: Scientists counted over 4,100 tiny animals living inside 244 deep-sea rock nodules in the Pacific. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Can Barbershops Turn Trust Into Better Health for Black Men?
item.description: Barbershops on Staten Island are offering health checks to Black men in a setting they already trust. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Get your blood pressure checked; many pharmacies do it free. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: An ancient virus may help explain what makes the human brain different
item.description: Researchers found an ancient virus may have helped shape how the human brain develops. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: This Tourette’s wrist device cut tics by a quarter in a UK trial
item.description: A wrist device cut tics by a quarter on average in a UK trial for Tourette's. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: They Became Pen Pals as Teens, Now 32 Years Later They’re Happily Married
item.description: Two teens who became pen pals on a Greek holiday in 1994 are now married. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Vitamin C could help block cancer-linked chemicals in your stomach, study finds
item.description: A model suggests vitamin C taken with meals may stop some cancer-linked chemicals forming in the stomach. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: A simple supplement could help your immune system fight cancer and viral infections
item.description: Researchers found the amino acid arginine helps immune cells fight cancer and viruses in early tests. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Dinosaurs may have been eating seaweed 100 million years ago
item.description: Fossil teeth suggest some dinosaurs ate seaweed and other ocean food 100 million years ago. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Euclid discovers ancient cosmic beacons from the dawn of time, shining like a trillion suns
item.description: The Euclid telescope found 31 ancient quasars, including two record holders from the early universe. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: SpaceX successfully catches top of huge Starship rocket for first time
item.description: SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship rocket in mid-air for the first time, a step toward reuse. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: A giant icy world hiding beyond Pluto could be our sixth dwarf planet
item.description: Astronomers found a large icy world beyond Pluto that could become the sixth known dwarf planet. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Maui Is Becoming a Living Laboratory for Regenerative Tourism
item.description: Visitors to Maui are helping restore land and reefs as the island rebuilds after the 2023 fires. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: When you travel, spend a day on local volunteering such as tree planting or a beach cleanup. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: How two Princeton graduates built the world’s first microplastics removal system
item.description: Two graduates built a system that filters microplastics from wastewater before it reaches rivers. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Crows can make decisions twice as fast as humans, scientists discover
item.description: Crows make visual decisions in 235 milliseconds, about twice as fast as humans. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
item.description: AI is helping a blind man with a brain implant see more precise shapes of light. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: A butterfly that fooled scientists for 200 years finally reveals its secrets
item.description: A familiar tropical butterfly turned out to be three species, one of them new to science. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Imagining the Mossy Cities of the Future
item.description: A moss wall built in Aachen to save a tree is inspiring plans for cooler, cleaner city streets. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Colleges Are Getting Creative to Help Students With Kids
item.description: Colleges are adding childcare, play spaces and flexible help so student parents can finish degrees. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: In Alaska’s capital, food comes by water, air or, most often, community sharing
item.description: In Juneau, where little can be farmed, neighbours keep each other fed by sharing fish, game and harvests. How you can help: Share surplus from your garden or kitchen with a neighbour. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: The Montana Ranch Where Autistic People Are Wranglers and Guides
item.description: A Montana guest ranch employs autistic adults as guides, wranglers and cooks. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: ‘It’s all God’s creation’: farmers continue a ‘Jewishly inspired’ agrarian tradition
item.description: A growing number of Jewish Americans are finding community through small farms rooted in tradition. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: How to move 1,300 plants for Kew's Palm House mega makeover
item.description: Kew is moving 1,300 plants so its historic Palm House can be restored. Source: BBC Science & Environment.
